text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today as oil prices retreated following diplomatic developments between the U.S. and Iran. After hitting $129.34 yesterday, the stock dropped to $127.30 as crude oil weakened—U.S. oil fell to $96.41 per barrel from higher levels earlier in the week. The shift came as Iran's foreign minister signaled openness to talks while the U.S. rejected Iran's ceasefire proposal, reducing near-term geopolitical risk premium that had been supporting energy prices.

Over the past two weeks, COP is down 7.3%, reflecting a broader softening in oil demand expectations. The wide gap between U.S. crude ($96.41) and global benchmark Brent ($114.89) suggests refining margins remain compressed, which pressures integrated oil companies' profit potential even as global prices stay elevated—a reminder that rising crude alone doesn't guarantee gains for energy stocks.
